title: Silent authz denial when service token lacks delegated permission
answers: Why does a label-selector LIST return an empty list with 200 OK instead of an error?
Search/list results are empty for dashboards, folders or variables even though data exists
authz check is denied without ever hitting the authz service
grafana_grpc_authz_limited_client_missing_delegated_permission_total is firing, what does it mean?
body:
Symptom: a label-selector LIST (dashboards, folders, variables) quietly returns an empty list with HTTP 200 instead of results or an error; nothing is logged.
Root cause: authlib's CheckServicePermissions (authz/service_permissions.go) denies the check locally when the calling service's token has no delegated permission for that group/resource/verb, so the authz service is never asked — this denial is indistinguishable from a real 'user has no access'.
Fix pattern: before delegating a Check/Compile/BatchCheck to the underlying authz client, call a guard (authzLimitedClient.serviceCanDelegate in pkg/storage/unified/resource/access.go) that detects this specific case and fails loudly (ErrServiceCannotDelegate) with a log line and a per-group/resource/verb counter, instead of letting the empty/denied result pass through silently.
Constraints: only applies when the identity's token carries some permissions but not the one being exercised; identities with no token permissions at all (single-tenant/in-process callers) are intentionally left alone since the underlying client already handles that case correctly.
applies: Any caller going through authzLimitedClient in pkg/storage/unified/resource for Check/Compile/BatchCheck
